Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the clear recap. Quick answers below — these are measured end-to-end from our dashboard (NYC clients) and include client network and our edge routing.
- p95 (end-to-end): ~480 ms
- p99 (end-to-end): ~920 ms
- typical request payload: 450 tokens (prompt+expected generation ~200-250 tokens, but we measure at 450 to be conservative)
- sustained throughput: 18 req/s during business hours; we see spikes to ~65 req/s during peak (concurrent streams ~40)
- streaming requirements: yes — token-level streaming required for chat; first token ideally <200 ms end-to-end

We've attached a short CSV export of recent latency percentiles and a sample request/response trace (sanitized).

We'd be interested in a short hosted bench to compare p95/p99 head-to-head. We can open a short test window next Wednesday morning (Aug 31) 9-11am ET. Let us know if that works and what endpoints you need to run the test.

Thanks,
Daniel

Aug 31 9-11am ET works for us. We'll upload the sample traces and CSV to the Drive link by EOD Monday (Aug 30). A few clarifications:
- Our p95/p99 numbers above are measured end-to-end from the browser client through our infra to the provider and back.

- We prefer the bench to run against a stable hosted endpoint (no autoscaling during the 10-min ramps) to reduce noise.
